newsitem.title: UK: Lira volatility rises as traders eye options.
newsitem.headline: Lira volatility rises as traders eye options.

text.p: The price of options to sell lire for German marks at a future date rose sharply here on Tuesday amid growing market concerns about Italy's possible omission from the first wave of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The lira skidded almost half a percentage point on the spot market to within a whisker of its European exchange rate mechanism (ERM) central rate at 990 per mark.
Both currency and bond markets were hit by comments on Monday from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and reported comments today from Belgian central bank chief Alfons Verplaetse.
Dealers said the Bank of Italy monitored prices closely as the lira approached 990 and they said it was prepared to sell marks on a move above this level.
Traders said actual transactions in lira options were quite subdued but the nervous spot market had boosted implied volatility levels, the key measure of options prices.

Implied volatility on one-week options rose as high as 6.50/7.50 percent compared with 5.50 percent late last week. Implied vol was up between 0.4/0.5 points overnight on one- and three-month options to more than six percent.

"The vol price is moving in tandem with the spot and with any spot risks in mark/lira still heavily skewed to a push higher on the cross, any rise in spot will drag vols higher with it," said Sara Sullivan, senior manager at HSBC's global FX options sales.

The one-month risk reversal, which is the premium on one-month mark calls against the lira over one-month mark puts, is currently skewed as much as 0.8/1.2 percentage points. Mark calls are a right to buy marks and puts a right to sell.

"Options interest in the cross has been quiet but that's probably because we saw such good resistance up around 990," said a trader at the FINEX futures and options exchange in Dublin. "It would really need to break 990 to take out some existing positions."
Dealers said a number of at-the-money mark calls were sold at the intraday highs today just below 990.

Others said that while a break of 990 would trigger a reversal of a number of short-term range strategies, most of the longer-term knockout options would remain intact unless 1,000 per mark were broken.
The latest jitters about Italy being out of the first wave of EMU, meantime, were stoked by what analysts said seemed a barbed meeting between Prodi and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
Prodi said on Monday Germany was less committed to EMU that Italy. "We see our future in Europe. I don't know if that is the case in Germany," he said.

"Prodi's exasperation at Kohl yesterday seems to show he suspects a plot against Italy joining in the first wave and the comments from Belgium today suggest the EU core is ganging up against Italy," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at Dutch bank ABN Amro in London

Belgian newspaper De Financieel Economische Tijd quoted Verplaetse as saying: "I would not mind seeing countries with a government deficit of seven percent (of gross domestic product) lowering their deficit to three percent in a year's time and in a durable way. In my view, that is not possible."
Verplaetse later denied his comments referred to Italy.

"The lira is the currency most vulnerable to a shift in EMU confidence in 1997, but this may have to wait until the latter half of the year when the debt and deficit picture is clearer," said Joe Prendergast, currency strategist at Merrill Lynch.

Prendergast said long positions in out-of-the-money mark calls were favoured to beneifit from this risk, given their high sensitivity to a surge in volatility back to the upper end of its long-term trading range and their relatively low time decay.
In the interim, Bank of Italy support and dollar strength should keep the lira's notional 2.25 percent ERM bands intact between 968 and 1012.5 per mark, he said.

As a result, Merrill recommend buying a 12-month mark call with a strike at 1050 and with double knockout levels at 965 and 1015 active for the first three months. The indicative cost of this strategy is 0.45 percent of the mark amount, he said.

On the spot market, analysts said a way to exploit lira weakness is to buy dollars for lira, taking advantage of dollar strength against European currencies and further potential lira weakness against the mark. The dollar/lira has surged 11.5 percent since the start of the year.
